problem_type: Canvas drag lease release assumes requestAnimationFrame in non-browser test hosts
symptom: The canvas dragging flag test reports an unhandled TypeError when the headless window fixture does not expose window.requestAnimationFrame.
direct_cause: The gesture-end guard called window.requestAnimationFrame directly even though the shared drag lease is also exercised by non-browser and reduced-window hosts.
class_root: The drag lease boundary had no host-safe scheduling adapter for the deferred release guard.
affected_population: Canvas pointer and resize gesture cleanup in reduced or headless window hosts
Vitest and future non-browser consumers of the shared drag lease
internal_only_reason: The scheduler fallback is an application-owned host boundary; browser requestAnimationFrame semantics are used when available and the deferred timer is only a compatibility path for reduced hosts.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The canvasDraggingFlag module owns the lease lifecycle and is the only place that schedules the deferred end guard; its focused test covers the lease ordering and cancellation contract.

invariants: A matching drag lease release remains deferred until queued lease releases have run, regardless of whether the host provides requestAnimationFrame.
Browser hosts continue to use requestAnimationFrame while reduced hosts use an asynchronous timer without changing lease ownership semantics.

door_reduction.why_not: The lease lifecycle has six write callers and fifteen read callers by design; this fix changes only the shared deferred scheduling boundary and does not merge independent gesture owners or host consumers.

generality_proof: All drag and resize callers already converge on CanvasDragLease; the scheduler adapter is selected at the shared release guard, so every caller gets identical ordering on browser and reduced hosts.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own drag lease state and schedule deferred matching-release cleanup across host capabilities.

recurrence.reason: Any reduced host can omit browser scheduling globals while exercising the shared drag lease.
same_class_scan: Checked all listed drag lease readers and writers.

prevention.invariant: Deferred matching-release cleanup always uses an asynchronous scheduler available to the current host.
prevention.failure_mode: A host without requestAnimationFrame no longer throws; the release guard still runs after prior lease releases.
prevention.strategy: Keep host capability detection in the shared lease module so gesture callers do not grow per-host fallbacks.

legacy_paths.rationale: The shared CanvasDragLease remains the only drag lifecycle path; only its scheduler capability branch was hardened.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency is added or upgraded; the fallback uses the host timer already available to the runtime.

migration: No persisted data or public caller contract changes.
residual_risks: Packaged browser visual evidence remains part of the release lane; browser hosts continue using requestAnimationFrame.
